_doc: Story 4.1 GOLDEN FIXTURE — the LOAD-BEARING rounding-mode pin (4.1-GOLDEN-01, R-402). Pins representative (quantity, unitPriceOre) -> expected lineNetOre cases under the CONSERVATIVE PILOT policy: LINE-LEVEL rounding with a single half-rounding mode = ROUND-HALF-AWAY-FROM-ZERO (Math.round semantics on non-negative inputs; x.5 -> x+1). The `.5`-boundary cases DISTINGUISH half-away-from-zero from half-to-even/banker's rounding: `expectedLineNetOre` is the pinned (half-up) value and `bankersWouldGive` records the DIFFERENT value banker's rounding would produce — so an accidental flip to half-to-even FAILS LOUD against this fixture. Each case carries an `origin` label. Money numbers only — NO PII (NFR17/R-411). This rounding policy is a CONSERVATIVE PILOT ASSUMPTION pending owner/accounting sign-off; it is NOT accounting-final (architecture.md#10 Rounding; test-design-epic-4 Sign-Off Q1).

lineNetCases.note: 0.5 * 5 = 2.5 oere exactly. half-away-from-zero -> 3; banker's (round-half-to-even) -> 2 (2 is even). The load-bearing distinguisher: a mode flip here fails loud.
0.5 * 45 = 22.5 oere exactly. half-away-from-zero -> 23; banker's -> 22 (22 is even). Second independent .5-boundary distinguisher.
0.333 * 100000 = 33300 oere (no rounding residue). A fractional quantity produces a deterministic exact oere result.
2.25 * 333 = 749.25 oere -> rounds down to 749 under either mode (not a .5 boundary); guards the general round-to-nearest path.
3 * 79000 = 237000 oere exact (2 370,00 kr). Large-value guard; integer oere stays exact (well under ORE_AMOUNT_MAX).

sumOfRoundedCase.note: Three identical lines of (0.5 * 45 = 22.5 -> 23). Totals must SUM the already-rounded line values (sum-of-rounded), NOT round the raw sum. sum-of-rounded = 23*3 = 69; round-of-sum would be Math.round(67.5) = 68. The engine must yield 69.
